# {.divider data-background-color="#0B1F3A"}

::: {.eyebrow}
Section 1
:::

## What is an Antibody? {.divider}

::: {.columns}

::: {.column width="60%"}

The immune system's job is to distinguish *self* from *non-self* — and to neutralize anything foreign. Antibodies are the precision instruments it uses to do that.

::: {.card}
::: {.card-title}
Y-shaped protein
:::
::: {.card-body}
Produced by B cells. Two binding sites at the tips of the Y.
:::
:::

::: {.card}
::: {.card-title}
Recognises an antigen
:::
::: {.card-body}
The molecular target the antibody binds.
:::
:::

::: {.card}
::: {.card-title}
Binds at an epitope
:::
::: {.card-body}
The specific 5–20 aa region of the antigen actually contacted.
:::
:::

:::

::: {.column width="40%"}

::: {.stat}
::: {.stat-number}
~10^15^
:::
::: {.stat-label}
unique antibodies the immune system can, in principle, produce
:::
:::

:::

:::

# From DNA to Antibodies & Antigens {.divider data-background-color="#0B1F3A"}

::: {.eyebrow}
Section 2
:::

## [§2.1]{.eyebrow-small} The Central Dogma as the Starting Point

*Both antibodies and antigens are proteins — and proteins are the end product of the same fundamental biological process.*

::: {.flow}
::: {.step .s1}
::: {.step-name} DNA :::
::: {.step-sub} encoded sequence :::
:::
::: {.chev} ▸ :::
::: {.step .s2}
::: {.step-name} RNA :::
::: {.step-sub} transcribed :::
:::
::: {.chev} ▸ :::
::: {.step .s3}
::: {.step-name} Peptide :::
::: {.step-sub} translated · amino acids :::
:::
::: {.chev} ▸ :::
::: {.step .s4}
::: {.step-name} Protein :::
::: {.step-sub} folded · functional :::
:::
:::

::: {.panel}
::: {.panel-title}
A note on peptide vs protein
:::
A peptide is a short amino acid chain; a protein is a longer, folded one. The distinction is one of length and structural complexity, not kind. Antigens and antibodies are both proteins — what differs is their origin, function, and the immune logic that connects them.
:::

## [§2.2]{.eyebrow-small} What is an Antigen?

*Any molecule — almost always a protein or a fragment of one — that the immune system can recognize and respond to.*

::: {.col-cards}
::: {.ccard}
::: {.tag} Pathogens :::
::: {.body} Viral coat proteins, bacterial surface proteins, toxins :::
:::
::: {.ccard}
::: {.tag} The host itself :::
::: {.body} In autoimmunity, the immune system generates antibodies against its own proteins :::
:::
::: {.ccard}
::: {.tag} Environmental :::
::: {.body} Allergens — pollen, food proteins, and other exogenous triggers :::
:::
:::

::: {.panel .dark}
::: {.panel-eyebrow} Key insight :::
::: {.panel-title}
Antibody reactivity is fundamentally a peptide-level phenomenon — even when the antigen is a full-length protein.
:::
The immune system responds to specific regions — *epitopes* — typically short stretches of 5–20 amino acids that happen to be physically accessible and structurally recognizable.
:::

## [§2.3]{.eyebrow-small} What is an Antibody, Molecularly Speaking?

*An antibody is a protein, encoded in DNA, produced by B cells. The remarkable thing is how its antigen-binding region comes into being.*

::: {.columns}

::: {.column width="50%"}

**V(D)J Recombination**

Antibody genes are not fixed in the germline. Gene segments are randomly shuffled and joined within B cells.

::: {style="display:flex;gap:0.4em;margin:0.6em 0;"}
::: {style="background:#065A82;color:#fff;width:2.5em;height:2em;border-radius:4px;text-align:center;line-height:2em;font-weight:700;font-size:1.4em;"}
V
:::
::: {style="background:#1C7293;color:#fff;width:2.5em;height:2em;border-radius:4px;text-align:center;line-height:2em;font-weight:700;font-size:1.4em;"}
D
:::
::: {style="background:#F2A413;color:#fff;width:2.5em;height:2em;border-radius:4px;text-align:center;line-height:2em;font-weight:700;font-size:1.4em;"}
J
:::
:::

*…randomly shuffled & joined*

:::

::: {.column width="50%"}

**…then Mutation & Selection**

Rounds of somatic mutation refine binding affinity in response to antigen exposure across the organism's lifetime.

::: {.panel}
::: {.panel-title}
Biographically informative
:::
The antibody sequence is partly determined by the genome and partly by a stochastic, exposure-driven process — making the reactome biographically informative in a way the genome alone is not.
:::

:::

:::

## [§2.4]{.eyebrow-small} How the DNA → Peptide → Protein Chain Enables Measurement

*Because every protein is ultimately encoded in DNA, an immunological binding experiment can be converted into a sequencing experiment.*

::: {.proc-grid}

::: {.proc}
::: {.num} 1 :::
::: {.body}
::: {.t} Design in silico :::
::: {.b} Take any set of protein sequences (proteome, viral, allergens), tile into overlapping peptides, synthesize the corresponding DNA computationally. :::
:::
:::

::: {.proc}
::: {.num} 2 :::
::: {.body}
::: {.t} Express from DNA :::
::: {.b} Cell-free transcription and translation produce the actual peptide or protein library in the lab. :::
:::
:::

::: {.proc}
::: {.num} 3 :::
::: {.body}
::: {.t} Attach DNA barcode :::
::: {.b} MIPSA self-assembly covalently links a unique DNA identifier to each expressed protein. :::
:::
:::

::: {.proc}
::: {.num} 4 :::
::: {.body}
::: {.t} Read out by sequencing :::
::: {.b} Antibody-bound antigens (and their barcodes) are pulled down. Sequencing the barcodes tells you which antigens were bound, and in what quantity. :::
:::
:::

:::

::: {.takeaway}
The measurement currency is DNA throughout — the biology happens in the middle, but the bookkeeping is entirely nucleotide-based.
:::

# What is the Antibody Reactome? {.divider data-background-color="#0B1F3A"}

::: {.eyebrow}
Section 3
:::

## [§3]{.eyebrow-small} What is the Antibody Reactome?

::: {.columns}

::: {.column width="55%"}

The complete set of antigen-binding reactivities present in a biological sample — typically blood serum or plasma — at a given point in time.

::: {.panel}
::: {.panel-title}
A snapshot of immunological history
:::
- Every pathogen encountered
- Every vaccine received
- Every self-protein mistakenly targeted
- Every allergen that triggered a response
:::

*If the genome is the blueprint and the transcriptome is what's being expressed, the reactome is a record of exposures and responses — written in the language of binding specificities.*

:::

::: {.column width="45%"}

::: {.eyebrow-small}
For a data scientist
:::

**A high-dimensional, sparse count matrix**

# Why is it Interesting? {.divider data-background-color="#0B1F3A"}

::: {.eyebrow}
Section 4
:::

## [§4.1]{.eyebrow-small} An Omic with Memory

::: {.columns}

::: {.column width="50%"}

Unlike gene expression, which fluctuates with conditions, **antibody reactivities are relatively durable**.

*An infection years ago can leave a detectable antibody signature today.*

::: {.panel .dark}
::: {.panel-eyebrow} Unusual among omics :::
::: {.panel-title}
The reactome carries longitudinal information in a cross-sectional measurement.
:::
:::

:::

::: {.column width="50%"}

```{=html}
<div style="padding-left:1em;">
  <div style="font-weight:700;font-size:0.95em;color:#5C6B7A;">Gene expression</div>
  <div style="font-style:italic;font-size:0.78em;color:#5C6B7A;margin-bottom:0.3em;">fluctuates with conditions</div>

              fill="none" stroke="#5C6B7A" stroke-width="2"/>
  </svg>

  <div style="font-style:italic;font-size:0.78em;color:#5C6B7A;margin-bottom:0.3em;">durable — exposures leave persistent signatures</div>
```

:::

:::

## [§4.2]{.eyebrow-small} Encodes Exposure History at Population Scale

*At the population level, the reactome is a rich epidemiological signal.*

::: {.col-cards .centered}

::: {.ccard}
::: {.num} 1 :::
::: {.tag} Pathogen exposure :::
::: {.body} Which pathogens has a community been exposed to? Reactivity patterns across individuals reveal community-level infection histories. :::
:::

::: {.ccard}
::: {.num} 2 :::
::: {.tag} Vaccine effectiveness :::
::: {.body} Which vaccines are working? Antibody signatures track real-world immune response, not just intended response. :::
:::

::: {.ccard}
::: {.num} 3 :::
::: {.tag} Demographic clustering :::
::: {.body} How do immune responses cluster across age, geography, and other demographic groups? :::
:::

:::

::: {.takeaway}
Patterns of reactivity across individuals → community-scale immunological insight.
:::

## [§4.3]{.eyebrow-small} Can Detect Disease — Including Before Symptoms

::: {.columns}

::: {.column width="45%"}

**Autoantibodies**

*Antibodies that mistakenly target the body's own proteins.*

::: {style="margin-top:1em;"}
**Associated diseases**

- Lupus
- Rheumatoid arthritis
- Certain cancers
- …and a wide range of others
:::

:::

::: {.column width="55%"}

**The early-detection window**

::: {.timeline}
::: {.label .early} Autoantibodies<br>appear :::
::: {.label .late} Clinical<br>diagnosis :::
::: {.line} :::
::: {.dot .early} :::
::: {.dot .late} :::
::: {.gap} ◀ years ▶ :::
:::

::: {.panel}
The reactome is a candidate for early detection — **years before symptoms**.
:::

:::

:::

## [§4.4]{.eyebrow-small} It is a Hard Measurement Problem

*Until recently, measuring the antibody reactome comprehensively was not feasible. The breakthrough came with sequencing-based display methods.*

::: {.columns}

::: {.column width="50%"}
